pill.desc: clear, colorless to pale yellow solution in a pre-filled syringe

tell: A recombinant decoy receptor injected into the eye that traps VEGF-A and PlGF, made in CHO cells.

clues.text: Given into the eye for local effect; free drug in plasma is undetectable two weeks after dosing. It is cleared by target-mediated binding to free VEGF and by proteolysis.
Made in recombinant Chinese hamster ovary cells as a dimeric glycoprotein with a total mass of 115 kDa, supplied as a sterile, aqueous solution for intravitreal injection.
Approved under a BLA as a single-dose pre-filled syringe or vial, given every 4 weeks at first and then every 8 weeks.
No boxed warning; contraindicated with ocular or periocular infection, active intraocular inflammation or hypersensitivity. Conjunctival hemorrhage and eye pain are among the most common reactions.
Wet age-related macular degeneration, macular edema after retinal vein occlusion, diabetic macular edema and retinopathy, and retinopathy of prematurity.
Acts as a soluble decoy receptor that binds VEGF-A and PlGF, preventing their activation of VEGFR-1 and VEGFR-2 on endothelial cells.
The generic name begins with A and has eleven letters.
